content.comment_body: About 1.5 years ago, I submitted a bug report to [company_name] regarding an error in [product_name] [version_no] and earlier templates. They acknowledged it and promised to notify the development team. The issue resides in the runtimeTemplate.html (and also affects loginTemplate.html) under the installation directory. These files contain a meta tag intended to prevent certain browsers from caching webpage content, which is important for pages displaying constantly changing data. The tag appears as <meta http-equiv="" pragram "" content=""no-cache""/>, but the correct attribute should be "pragma," not "pragram." Browsers ignore "pragram." More info: [url]. Now, with [product_name] [version_no] released, they replaced "pragram" with "program"—which is not correct either. Is this the best outcome after a year and a half and several rounds of quality control? What happened, [company_name]?
[company_name] notes, upon upgrading to [product_name] [version_no], that there is an update for [product_name] to [version_no], specifically for AWS Tomcat.
The statement by [user_name] is accurate. Both files use "program" instead of "pragma." Refer to the screenshots.

HTML programming is not a feature of [product_name]. Users already have access to all data using the four default web pages provided by the Webserver. [product_name] generates HTML code for a graphical view of data. If you want more features or custom improvements, you can modify the code, but then you can't continue using [product_name]. Only HTML experts should attempt these changes.

That's a weak excuse. Just because something wasn't intended to be used doesn't mean it's justified. HTML isn't a programming language; it's just a standardized way to show documents on the web. The generated HTML is flawed due to template issues in [product_name], distributed by [company_name]. Anyone installing [product_name] will encounter incorrect meta tags. I filed a bug report years ago with a simple fix, but now it's replaced with another incorrect term. Also, [company_name] suggests you can freely modify the code for more features, but if so, why not make [product_name] open source and document the API for data transfer, starting/stopping functions, and access via Ethernet? If that's not possible, just be honest. [product_name] is marketed and priced as an industrial-grade tool, not a hobbyist device, so customers expect a more refined product. Thanks for reading.

It seems there was some confusion. We've discussed the matter with development again. "pragma" is a standard HTML keyword, used to instruct browsers not to cache page content locally. Once set, the page cannot be retrieved from the cache. This should be improved in the next version of [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: There has been a recurring issue in template files generated by [product_name], where incorrect use of meta tag keywords undermines proper HTML cache control. Although the bug and its straightforward fix were reported to [company_name] long ago, it remained unaddressed in multiple subsequent releases. Users voiced their dissatisfaction with the apparent lack of thorough quality assurance and delayed bug fixes, and found the responses from support unsatisfactory and lacking responsibility.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [company_name] to recognize and quickly resolve clear errors found in distributed product templates, release reliable updates, and uphold the high standards typical of industrial-grade software and hardware.
